label: quantum record (RECORDED archive shots: IBM hardware + legacy unlabelled; not live quantum)
what: Dice for sampling Zeref's replies, drawn from a compact table built from the WHOLE public quantum archive (phera-ra/QC67_cosmo @ b414724c): one parity bit per recorded shot, shuffled by a fixed modular permutation, so every roll traces to a recorded shot. The two-job dice (v1) is superseded; its jobs stay below as history. Not a live quantum connection, not a new measurement, and it does not change his brain.

table.shuffle: old = (i * 1000003) mod 11354129, skipping old >= 11354112; every shot appears exactly once
table.note: MSB was measured at 0.488630, too biased for a dice; parity is used instead. A plain round-robin interleave was measured and rejected: the canonical runs are aligned across records, so it began with 33,003 consecutive zeros.

shots_by_class.note: Every non-simulator shot in the archive feeds the table: verified IBM hardware rounds plus legacy unlabelled counts (provider metadata not retained; never counted as verified hardware provenance). The 1,024 Rigetti SIMULATOR shots are excluded. The classical-control rounds in the CHSH file are not in this archive.

history.note: v1 dice source, superseded by the full-loop table; kept as history, not deleted

sampler.turn_seed: sha256('zeref-qrec-turn-v1|' + record_seed + '|' + roll + '|' + prompt ids joined by ',')
sampler.uniform: 52 table bits at position int(sha256(turn_seed + '|' + k)[:13], 16) mod (11354112 - 52), / 2^52
sampler.provenance_note: Cory's HF card (phera-ra/QC67_cosmo) measured the decoder sampling seed as null for accuracy: the record buys replayable provenance and variety, not a smarter brain.
